newsitem.title: UK: Venezuela's Casas says strong bolivar important.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Casas says strong bolivar important.

text.p: Venezuela's central bank director said on Thursday that maintaining the strength of the bolivar was important in helping the country meet its 1996 inflation target.

"The important thing is to maintain it strong in order to fulfil our major target which is lower inflation," Antonia Casas Gonzalez told reporters after a speech to London financiers at the Bank of England.
"It won't affect our non-traditional exports," he added.
The Venezuelan currency was floated last May as part of an IMF-inspired economic reform programme.
The currency subsequently strengthened, and analysts say the country's success in fighting inflation means the currency is appreciating still further in real terms.

Recent strong capital inflows, boosted in part by windfall oil revenues, are swelling the country's reserves, boosting liquidity and impacting on the exchange rate. But Casas said Venezuela did not want to slap controls on these inflows.
"We want to avoid imposing controls if we can...we don't want to impose restrictions so the only way we can handle them is via our weekly auctions."
He said Venezuela did not want to follow the Brazilian example of sterilising strong capital inflows by issuing fresh debt. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
